title: Exclusive | 100-foot triangular UFO over Colorado base captured in video Air Force won't release: sources
excerpt: A pair of classified videos allegedly showing a 100-foot black triangular UFO over a Colorado military base remain locked away despite President Trump’s new order aimed at encouraging more UF…
content:
A pair of classified videos allegedly showing a 100-foot black triangular UFO over a Colorado military base remain locked away despite President Trump’s new order aimed at encouraging more UFO whistleblowers to come forward, sources familiar with the footage told The Post.

Two videos, recorded on a service member’s personal cellphone on consecutive nights in 2023, are among the pieces of evidence whistleblowers say still cannot be discussed or released publicly because they remain classified by the Air Force, sources said.

Those videos — which captured the craft zooming over mountains and actively camouflaging in clouds — are stored with the Air Force Office of Special Investigations in Colorado, file numbers IRR1669S015524 and IRR1669S005024, according to those sources.

Previous UFO whistleblowers warn that “nothing has changed” after Trump’s new order waiving nondisclosure agreements for more people with special knowledge on government programs to report to executive branch agencies — and that the best evidence is still behind a wall of classification.

“This does nothing for the people who could have come forward and spoken already,” Dylan Borland, a US Air Force Veteran and former private contractor, told The Post. “Nothing has changed.”

Borland testified to Congress in 2024 that he also witnessed a massive triangular UFO hovering over a NASA hangar for a few minutes without making a sound before rapidly ascending to the level of commercial jets in mere seconds.

“I’ve done the committees, done private meetings, at this point, unless I’m speaking under oath to the public, what’s the point?” Borland said.

Matthew Brown, a former defense industry contractor, came forward on the Weaponized Podcast in early 2026 to reveal to the public just some of what he told to Congress and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence behind closed doors — that there was a secret Pentagon program called “Immaculate Constellation” that studied, collected data and recovered UFOs.

“[Trump’s order] frankly doesn’t do anything new,” said Brown. “It does not free whistleblowers to speak publicly.”

Both Brown and Borland were on the receiving end of professional reprisals and character assassinations after they blew the whistle to AARO and ODNI.

Borland alleges he faced retaliation after blowing the whistle — including problems with his security clearance, workplace harassment and a derailed career.

Brown lost his job as a contractor and was smeared as an antisemite to reporters after he went through the proper channels of whistleblowing, he claimed on the Weaponized podcast.

“AARO and ODNI should not have any leadership role in this project as they have discredited themselves,” Brown stated.

Several more potential whistleblowers are unmoved by the Trump administration directive and are still holding back their testimonies and best evidence, according to sources.

Some, however, are supportive of the president.

“I welcome President Trump’s action and hope it gives courage to those who have said nondisclosure agreements prevented them from telling Congress or the Executive Branch what they know,” David Grusch, a former Air Force intelligence officer and UFO whistleblower, told The Post.

“I was the first whistleblower to file an Inspector General complaint alleging that these UAP legacy programs were being concealed from awful oversight, and I later testified under oath in both classified and public settings.

“I paid a severe personal and professional price for doing so. Others should not have to face the same barriers or retaliation to tell the truth.”
